 Cameron Johnson (ankle) is out for Saturday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Johnson sprained his right ankle during the second quarter of Thursday’s loss to the Thunder and did not return. Alpha Diallo started the third quarter, but he’s questionable for Saturday’s game. If Diallo can’t play, the Nuggets may turn to DeMar DeRozan from the start. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Cameron Johnson (ankle) finished Thursday’s loss to the Thunder with five points (2-of-3 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer. 
 Johnson played 11 minutes in Thursday’s opener before a right ankle injury ended his night just before halftime. Officially, the veteran wing was questionable for the second half, but he never returned. Alpha Diallo (4/2/3/1) started the second half and played 22 minutes. If Nuggets head coach David Adelman prefers to keep DeMar DeRozan in the sixth man role, Diallo could start Saturday’s game against the Pelicans if Johnson can’t play. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson (ankle) is questionable to return to Thursday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Johnson injured his right ankle during the first half of Thursday’s season opener and did not start the third quarter. Alpha Diallo started the period in Johnson’s place. If Johnson doesn’t return, Diallo and DeMar DeRozan stand to gain the most in playing time. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson finished Friday’s exhibition against the Lakers with 12 points (5-of-8 FGs), three rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers. 
 Johnson’s preseason ended with just over six minutes remaining in the third quarter after being assessed a Flagrant 2 foul for elbowing Lakers guard Austin Reaves in the chin. Both teams seemed shocked by the call, but the foul won’t carry over into the regular season from a punishment standpoint. Johnson’s first season in Denver was a struggle in terms of production and staying healthy, which has pushed his ADP outside the first 100 picks in Yahoo leagues. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson accounted for 15 points (5-of-7 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, one assist, two steals and four three-pointers in Sunday’s exhibition against the Bulls. 
 While Johnson’s production was expected to take a hit after his move to Denver, his debut season in the Mile High City was disappointing. In addition to the perimeter shooting struggles, availability was once again an issue for the veteran forward. Johnson has played 58 games or fewer in each of his last four seasons, another reason why he’s slipped down draft boards. While capable of offering top-100 value, fantasy managers can’t use that early of a pick on Johnson, given the recent history. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson added 27 points (8-of-15 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one block and five three-pointers in Thursday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 Johnson rose to the occasion on Thursday, logging one of his best performances of the season. Despite the loss, he drained half of his 10 three-point attempts, nearly pulled down double-digit rebounds, and finished as one of Denver’s most reliable scoring options on the evening. Johnson came into the season with some expectations to serve as the missing piece for the Nuggets, who acquired him via trade during the offseason. His production fluctuated throughout the season, and he ultimately averaged just 12.2 points overall, his lowest since his sophomore season. A more effective season and better fantasy production should be expected in Year 2 with the Nuggets next season.

 Murray, Braun and Johnson will remain out for Sunday’s regular-season finale. Tyus Jones, Bruce Brown and Julian Strawther started Friday’s win over the Thunder, and all should get another start on Sunday. For those in active leagues who need scoring, Strawther may be the best option to slot into fantasy lineups.

 Absent from the initial report released by the Nuggets, Johnson is now questionable for injury management reasons. If he does not play against the Thunder, Tim Hardaway Jr. stands to benefit the most among the available reserves. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson tallied 18 points (8-of-12 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers on Wednesday in the win over the Grizzlies. 
 Johnson was one of several Nuggets players to produce on the offensive end against the Grizzlies. Specifically, he was one of eight to finish with double-digit points, utilizing efficient shooting from beyond the arc and success inside the three-point line to conclude as the team’s second-leading scorer. After a slow start to the season regarding three-point shooting, Johnson has really picked it up and turned in an efficient season. His scoring uptick in April could prove to be valuable with the playoffs just around the corner. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson accounted for 17 points (6-of-11 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist, two blocks and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Spurs. 
 Johnson has now made multiple three-pointers in seven consecutive games, providing the consistent production in that category that was absent for significant stretches earlier this season. Better late than never for those who stuck with the Nuggets wing throughout this season. For those whose leagues run through the end of the regular season, Denver plays four games in Week 24, starting with the Trail Blazers on Monday.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo had 36 points (15-of-26 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Pistons. 
 Antetokounmpo has now had at least 35 points in each of his first two games in a Heat uniform. He played a more complete game across the stat sheet compare to the opener with 12 rebounds, five assists and three stocks. Still, the Heat lost to the Pistons by 17 after dropping the opener to the Timberwolves by 25. Miami will look for its first win of the season and probably get it against the reeling Hornets in Charlotte on Saturday.

 Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff told reporters there’s no injury update on Ausar Thompson (ankle) and Jalen Duren (thigh). 
 Thompson appeared to roll his ankle while Duren grabbed his leg and headed to the locker room midway through the second quarter. While there was no update from Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff after the game, the team said Duren was questionable to return with a thigh injury. It’s unclear if either player will be available for Sunday’s game against the 76ers, though more information about Thompson and Duren’s status should be available Saturday.

 Duncan Robinson had 17 points (5-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, two assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Heat. 
 Robinson is yet to make a two-point field goal so far this season, but he’s 10-of-19 from behind the three-point line in the first two games this year. The 32-year-old forward’s fantasy utility is mostly limited to his three-point shooting, but it looks like the right time to continue to ride the hot hand.

 John Collins had 23 points (9-of-15 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers against the Heat on Friday. 
 Collins had a quiet debut with six points in the win over the Celtics on Tuesday, but he was excellent in the win over the Heat on Friday. The 29-year-old power forward was 9-of-15 from the field, including 5-of-6 from behind the three-point line. Jalen Duren (thigh) left with an injury in the second quarter and didn’t return, which likely led to more opportunities for Collins. With Duren’s status still up in the air, Collins could be in line for more usage again on Sunday against the 76ers. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Cade Cunningham

 Cade Cunningham had 16 points (5-of-8 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, eight assists, one steal, three blocks and two three-pointers in the Pistons’ 128-111 victory over the Heat on Friday. 
 Cunningham had another fine game as he filled the stat sheet and led the Pistons to another win to start the season. However, after turning the ball over five times in the win over the Celtics on Tuesday, he had seven turnovers against the Heat on Friday. Even opposing coaches like the Heat’s Erik Spolstra have pointed out that Cunningham isn’t necessarily a bad ball-handler, but commits a lot of turnovers thanks to almost always having the ball in his hands. That doesn’t offer much comfort to fantasy managers with Cunningham in nine-category leagues as he’s likely to be towards the top of the league in turnovers this year. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Brandon Miller had six points (2-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Hawks on Friday. 
 There’s no sugarcoating it; Miller is off to a rough start to begin the season. The 23-year-old small forward had 18 points in the opener, but shot just 7-of-21 from the floor. He followed that performance up by going 2-of-14, including 1-of-11 from behind the three-point line. He’s now 4-of-25 (16 percent) from behind the arc to begin the season. Miller was an almost incomprehensible -37 in 22 minutes in the 128-81 loss to the Haws Friday. Is this rock bottom? Because it feels like it can only get better from here. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Naz Reid had 17 points (7-of-16 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Reid had seven turnovers despite only playing 24 minutes and that’s a crusher in nine-category leagues. Otherwise, he’s scored 37 points on 15-of-34 attempts with seven three-pointers in his first two games with the Hornets. That’ll play. If Reid can keep the turnovers under control, he’s well on his way to paying off his mid-round draft price.

 Miles McBride produced 20 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and six three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 McBride rebounded nicely from his poor showing in Tuesday’s loss to the 76ers, a game in which he scored three points on 1-of-5 shooting. Against the Celtics, Deuce shot 6-of-8 from three and scored 20 of the Knicks’ 32 bench points. The reserve role doesn’t help McBride deliver consistent fantasy value, but he can be an effective source of points and three-pointers in deep leagues.

 Jalen Brunson accumulated 19 points (7-of-17 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Brunson’s gotten off to a slow start by his standards, shooting 13-of-32 from the field in New York’s first two games. The Knicks star also didn’t shoot well from the foul line, missing three of his six attempts in Boston. Those rostering Brunson don’t have much to worry about, as the season is only two games old. However, they would certainly like to see him clean up his shooting in Sunday’s game against the Magic.
